item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So an alternate universe/alien Foundation is examining a laptop from "our neck of the woods". That's what I've gathered, and I like the execution in that it made the "ah-ha" moment of realizing that it was, in fact, just a laptop that much more satisfying while also accentuating the alien taste vs. sight means of analyzing what they'd found.

To be honest, though, the speculating I've done is much more exciting. To me, anyway, y'alls are welcome to shoot me down if my ideas aren't worth reading the ramble, which I've often found out the hard way.

So these aliens taste electromagnetism and radiation the same way we see it. Sounds almost like they're what we might think of as robots, or synthetic lifeforms if you prefer, that instead of being 'organic' lifeforms and developing 'synthetic' technology have started out as 'synthetic' and worked out 'organic' technology. I suppose that in this case, 'organic' and 'synthetic' become relative terms since the alternate universe conception of both would be reversed, seeing as that one refers to something that developed naturally and the other unnaturally. Hence they would see tech composed of metals and plastics, they're 'organic' compounds, as alien and weird in the same way we see their compact disks as strange, being composed of our 'organic' compounds.

Now, the real question is if this thing is related at all to SCP 003, the Biological Motherboard, and subsequently if their origins are similar. If there was ever a good reason to cross-test SCPs (and maybe get way the hell out of dodge), then this is it. There's plenty of unanswered questions surrounding the each individual SCP, after all.

item.title: Re: Nitpick about the text.
item.content:encoded:
:) It does describe a piece of Earth technology, yes. I don't want to give too much away until the article's been up a little longer.

Considering that the text is entirely romanised, I'm not sure why it would have to be in unicode. I mean, it could and there'd be nothing wrong with that, but both are just ways of encoding data in binary. My idea is that the original binary code is converted to ascii-compatible text by a decrypting algorithm. SCP-328-01-ARC (not real) contains that original document, which is written in several languages. SCP-328-01 is the same document with all the recognised languages converted into modern english.

Technically ASCII is a method of storing text using a set of English characters as binary, and not the set itself.

Compression makes more sense as a reason to obscure the data, in my opinion.
